merger_description:
LTM UK & Ireland Limited (**LTM**) proposes to acquire Randstad’s technology and consulting business in Europe and Australia, pursuant to a share agreement (the Acquisition).

The Acquisition of Randstad’s technology and consulting business in Australia involves acquiring 100% of the shares in FinXL Professional Services Pty Ltd (**FinXL**) from Randstad Digital Holdings Pty Ltd (**Randstad Digital**).

The acquirer, LTM, is a foreign company registered under the laws of England & Wales. It is a wholly owned subsidiary of LTM Limited. LTM Limited is a public company listed on BSE Limited and the National Stock Exchange of India Limited.

LTM is a global technology consulting and information technology services business. It provides a range of professional services across application management, cognitive infrastructure, cybersecurity, data and analytics, enterprise applications, business AI, transformation, and internet of things.

Randstad is a leading global talent company in the HR and recruitment services industry. Randstad also operates a technology and consulting business, which provides technology solutions and IT consulting services.

Randstad provides these services in Australia through Randstad Digital’s Australian entity, FinXL. FinXL provides technology solutions and IT consulting services in Australia and has a particular focus on data analytics, AI solutions, cloud and infrastructure, and digital and product engineering.

determination_table_content.details:
LTM UK & Ireland Limited (LTM) applied for a notification waiver in
respect of its proposed acquisition of Randstad’s technology and
consulting business in Europe and Australia, pursuant to a share
purchase agreement, as described in the transaction documents
provided as part of the application (the Acquisition).
The Acquisition of Randstad’s technology and consulting business in
Australia involves acquiring 100% of the shares in FinXL
Professional Services Pty Ltd (FinXL) from Randstad Digital
Holdings Pty Ltd (Randstad Digital).

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission has
determined under section 51ABV(1)(a) of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.

The acquirer, LTM, is a foreign company registered under the laws of
England & Wales. It is a wholly owned subsidiary of LTM Limited.
LTM Limited is a public company listed on BSE Limited and the
National Stock Exchange of India Limited.
LTM is a global technology consulting and information technology
services business. It provides a range of professional services
across application management, cognitive infrastructure,
cybersecurity, data and analytics, enterprise applications, business
AI, transformation, and internet of things.
Randstad is a leading global talent company in the HR and
recruitment services industry. The target is Randstad’s technology
and consulting business in Europe and Australia, which provides
technology solutions and IT consulting services in Europe and
Australia.
Randstad provides these services in Australia through Randstad
Digital’s Australian entity, FinXL. FinXL provides technology solutions
and IT consulting services in Australia and has a particular focus on
data analytics, AI solutions, cloud and infrastructure, and digital and
product engineering.
Both parties supply IT consulting services, infrastructure
implementation and management services, and application
implementation and management services.

In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
certain publicly available information, and had regard to the factors
in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition and Consumer Act 2010
(Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information currently before it, the ACCC considers that
the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material lessening of
competition. In particular:
a. there is a small horizontal overlap between LTM and FinXL in
the supply of IT consulting services, infrastructure
implementation and management services and application
implementation and management services in Australia, and
the increase in share of supply arising from the Acquisition
for each of these services would be small
b. there are alternative suppliers of IT consulting services,
infrastructure implementation and management services,
and application implementation and management services
in Australia.
The ACCC has also had regard to the likelihood that, if the
Acquisition were put into effect, the notification thresholds
determined under section 51ABP(1) of the Act would apply.
While the ACCC considers that the notification thresholds are likely
to be met, given that material competition concerns are unlikely to
arise, the ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required
to be notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s interim guidance on
notification waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
